## Where we are

::: {.incremental}
- Session 1: spatial data, CRS, joins, honest maps
- Every spatial test asks: **are neighbouring areas more alike than chance?**
- First we must **define "neighbour"**. That definition is the **spatial weights matrix**, the most influential choice in the analysis
- By the end you can:
  - build **queen, rook, k-nearest** and **distance** neighbours
  - turn them into **row-standardised weights**
  - compute and read a **spatial lag**
  - check how sensitive a result is to the choice
:::

# Topic 1 — Who is a neighbour? {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Contiguity: share a boundary

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Rook:** share an **edge**
- **Queen:** share an edge **or a corner** (the usual default)
- Needs polygons; areas of similar size behave best
- Watch for **islands**: areas with no neighbour
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
nb_q <- poly2nb(blocks, queen = TRUE,  snap = 1e-4)
nb_r <- poly2nb(blocks, queen = FALSE, snap = 1e-4)
c(queen_links = sum(card(nb_q)), rook_links = sum(card(nb_r)))
```
:::
:::

```{r}
summary(nb_q)
```

## Seeing the links

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
#| fig-height: 5.6
cen <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(blocks))
plot(st_geometry(blocks), border = "grey70", main = "Queen contiguity")
plot(nb_q, cen, add = TRUE, col = "red", pch = 19, cex = 0.4)
```

::: {.key}
Check three things in `summary()`: the **average number of neighbours** (about 5 here), the **least and most connected** blocks, and any **isolates** (they break most tests unless `zero.policy = TRUE`).
:::

## Distance and k-nearest neighbours

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
#| fig-width: 11
knn5 <- knn2nb(knearneigh(cen, k = 5))
d <- unlist(nbdists(knn2nb(knearneigh(cen, k = 1)), cen))
nb_d <- dnearneigh(cen, 0, max(d))
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(st_geometry(blocks), border = "grey80", main = "5 nearest neighbours"); plot(knn5, cen, add = TRUE, col = "blue", pch = 19, cex = 0.3)
plot(st_geometry(blocks), border = "grey80", main = "Distance band"); plot(nb_d, cen, add = TRUE, col = "darkgreen", pch = 19, cex = 0.3)
```

| Definition | Neighbours per area | Good for | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Queen / rook | varies | polygons of similar size | islands; large areas have many neighbours |
| k nearest | exactly k | unequal areas, points | links across a gap that are not real |
| Distance band | varies | points, a travel-distance idea | too short: isolates; too long: everyone linked |

# Topic 2 — From neighbours to weights {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## A neighbour list says who; weights say how much

| Style | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"B"` binary | 1 for every neighbour |
| `"W"` **row-standardised** | each area's weights sum to 1; the usual choice |
| `"S"` | variance-stabilising |

```{r}
lw <- nb2listw(nb_q, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)
lw$weights[[1]]
sum(lw$weights[[1]])
```

::: {.key}
With `"W"`, area *i* gives each of its *k* neighbours weight 1/*k*. An area with 2 neighbours weights each by 0.5; one with 8 by 0.125.
:::

## The spatial lag

::: {.eq}
lag(x)~i~ = Σ~j~ w~ij~ x~j~ = **the average of i's neighbours**
:::

```{r}
blocks$lag_rate <- lag.listw(lw, blocks$dengue_per_100k, zero.policy = TRUE)
c(lag_from_function = blocks$lag_rate[1], mean_of_neighbours = mean(blocks$dengue_per_100k[nb_q[[1]]]))
```

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
#| fig-width: 11
p1 <- ggplot(blocks) + geom_sf(aes(fill = dengue_per_100k)) + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, name = NULL) + labs(title = "Rate")
p2 <- ggplot(blocks) + geom_sf(aes(fill = lag_rate)) + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, name = NULL) + labs(title = "Spatial lag (neighbours' average)")
p1 + p2
```

The lag is **smoother** than the original. Moran's I (Session 3) is essentially the slope of the lag on the value.

# Topic 3 — Does the choice matter? {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Sensitivity

```{r}
w_list <- list(queen = nb2listw(nb_q, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE), rook = nb2listw(nb_r, style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE),
               knn5 = nb2listw(knn5, style = "W"), distance = nb2listw(nb_d, style = "W"))
map_dfr(w_list, \(w) { m <- moran.test(blocks$dengue_per_100k, w, zero.policy = TRUE); tibble(I = round(unname(m$estimate[1]), 3), p = signif(m$p.value, 2)) }, .id = "weights")
```

::: {.incremental}
- Here the pattern is strong, so the conclusion barely moves
- With a **weak** pattern the answer can change with the weights
- **Justify** the choice with the biology: how far does a mosquito, a patient or an exposure travel?
- **Report** the weights and check sensitivity
:::

## Common mistakes

::: {.bad}
- Using the default without saying which one
- Ignoring isolates (silently dropping areas) or areas with 15 neighbours
- Using contiguity for **points** (they have no boundaries)
- Computing distances in **degrees** instead of a projected CRS
:::

## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s2q1", "In row-standardised weights, what do the weights of one area add up to?",
         c("The number of neighbours of that area",
           "0, because the weights cancel out",
           "1, whatever the number of neighbours",
           "The area's value divided by its population"), answer = 3,
         explain = "Row-standardisation divides each neighbour's weight by the area's neighbour count, so every row sums to 1. That makes the lag a weighted average.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s2q2", "An area has 4 neighbours and row-standardised weights. What is its spatial lag?",
         c("The sum of its 4 neighbours' values",
           "The mean of its 4 neighbours' values",
           "Its own value minus the district mean",
           "The value of its single nearest neighbour"), answer = 2,
         explain = "With weights of 1/4 each, the lag is the plain average of the neighbours' values.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s2q3", "Why are queen contiguity neighbours a poor choice for point data such as patient homes?",
         c("Points tend to have more than ten neighbours each",
           "Queen contiguity needs the data in degrees, not in metres",
           "Points have no boundaries to share, so contiguity does not exist",
           "Contiguity can only be calculated for blocks with no missing data"), answer = 3,
         explain = "Contiguity is defined by shared polygon boundaries. For points, use k-nearest or distance-based neighbours.")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s2q4", "summary(nb) reports one region with no neighbours (an island). What is the safest response?",
         c("Delete the region quietly so that the test runs without a warning",
           "Give it the average value of the whole district to fill the gap",
           "Ignore it, since one single area will not change the results",
           "Check it is real, then link it sensibly or use zero.policy"), answer = 4,
         explain = "Isolates have no neighbours, so the lag is undefined. Look at the map, decide a justified link (for example k-nearest) or analyse with zero.policy and say so.")
```

## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("s2q5", "Moran's I is 0.48 with queen weights and 0.12 with a distance band of 3 km. What is the best conclusion?",
         c("It depends on the weights, so justify the choice and report sensitivity",
           "Queen weights are the standard choice, so the 3 km result can simply be ignored",
           "The two values should be averaged to give the true value of Moran's I",
           "The analysis has failed, so the test should be dropped from the report"), answer = 1,
         explain = "Different neighbour definitions can give different answers when the pattern is scale dependent. Report which weights you used, why, and what happens with others.")
```

## Score and take-home

**Your score: <span class="quiz-score"></span>**

::: {.incremental}
- Weights turn 'near' into numbers; **choose them deliberately**
- **Row-standardised** weights make the lag the **average of neighbours**
- Check **isolates** and areas with very many neighbours
- **Report** the weights and test sensitivity
:::
